model.type: percentile-ranked, multi-source composite — a transparent weighted model, not a trained ML predictor

sfr.label: Single-family homes
sfr.note: Owner-occupied and rental detached housing; the deepest and most liquid market, and the only class with a direct public price index.

townhome.label: Townhomes & attached
townhome.note: Attached for-sale product. Highly sensitive to zoning: missing-middle reform is what makes it buildable at all.

duplex.label: Duplex & 2-4 unit
duplex.note: Small multifamily: residential financing with commercial-style yield. Very little new supply is built, so existing stock is structurally scarce.

apartment.label: Apartment buildings (5+)
apartment.note: The class where supply matters most: 5+ unit permitting swings hard by cycle and a delivery wave can flatten rents for years. Rent-control regime is a direct policy risk.

industrial.label: Industrial & warehouse
industrial.note: Logistics demand tracks transportation and warehousing employment (NAICS 48-49). Land cost and entitlement speed decide whether it can actually be built.

datacenter.label: Data centers
datacenter.note: Sited on power price, power availability and hazard exposure far more than on population. Industrial electricity cost is weighted heavily and cheap-power metros dominate.

retail.label: Retail (strip & centers)
retail.note: Rooftops and household income drive sales; existing retail establishments per capita measure how saturated the trade area already is.

hospitality.label: Hotels & hospitality
hospitality.note: Accommodation employment (NAICS 72) is the closest public proxy for room-night demand. Hazard exposure matters more here — a hurricane season closes the asset.

restaurant.label: Restaurants & F&B
restaurant.note: Food-service demand follows daytime population and discretionary income. Establishment density signals how contested the market is.

office.label: Office
office.note: Structurally challenged post-2020: office-using employment can grow while space demand per worker falls, so treat a high score as 'least bad', not as a buy signal.

land.label: Land & development
land.note: Scored from the developer's side: permit velocity and a permissive entitlement climate are the asset. This is the one class where heavy construction raises the score.

hud_fmr.label: HUD Fair Market Rents
hud_fmr.error: inactive: needs a free HUD API token (https://www.huduser.gov/portal/dataset/fmr-api.html). Add it as the repository secret HUD_API_TOKEN to enable Fair Market Rents by bedroom count. The published workbook URL changes every fiscal year and is not stable enough to scrape.

mls.label: MLS (RESO Web API)
mls.error: inactive: MLS requires a licensed RESO Web API feed. Set MLS_RESO_BASE_URL and MLS_RESO_TOKEN repository secrets to enable. Public alternatives (FHFA repeat-sales HPI, Census permits, Zillow inventory/days-on-market) are used meanwhile.

acs.label: Census ACS 5-year
acs.error: inactive: needs a free Census API key. Request one at https://api.census.gov/data/key_signup.html and add it as the repository secret CENSUS_API_KEY to enable income, tenure, structure-type and unemployment metrics.

bea_gdp.label: BEA metro GDP
bea_gdp.error: inactive: needs a free BEA API key (https://apps.bea.gov/API/signup/). Add it as the repository secret BEA_API_KEY to enable metro GDP.
